title: Router reinforced by acceptances: decay vs history lock-in

hypothesis.statement: A router whose weights are cumulative means of acceptances readapts after an abrupt change in a time proportional to its whole history; with exponential decay (EWMA rate lambda) the time is fixed by lambda and independent of the history, at the price of a stationary loss that grows with lambda.

predictions.text: Single estimate, history T0 = 500: the number of tasks until the past weighs less than 10% is within 5% (or 2 tasks) of 4,500 without decay and of 230, 45, 22 and 11 with lambda = 0.01, 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2.
Two-route router: the median switch time without decay grows at least 3x when the history goes from T0 = 500 to T0 = 2,000, while with lambda = 0.05 it changes by less than 25%.
Two-route router, T0 = 500: the median switch time without decay is at least 3x that of lambda = 0.05.

Stationary regime (no change, 20,000 tasks): the acceptance rate with lambda <= 0.05 is within 5% (relative) of the router without decay, and the loss with lambda = 0.2 is larger than with lambda = 0.01 (disjoint 95% CIs).

params.rules: Estimate: T0 observations at p_good, then an abrupt change to p_bad; t90 = first task after the change at which the run-averaged estimate has covered 90% of the distance to the new value. Router: two routes, epsilon-greedy (explore uniformly with probability epsilon); cumulative policy keeps per-route mean with a prior of 1 acceptance in 2 trials; EWMA policy starts at 0.5 and updates only the chosen route. History: T0 tasks with route A at p_good and B at p_bad; then they swap. Switch time = first task after the swap from which the estimate of B stays above the estimate of A for `hold` consecutive tasks; censored at the horizon.
